try: Open {url}. The sidebar on the left lists the chats of this project, most recent first: "The hospital sent the discharge letter today." (no name yet: its first sentence), "invoices" (named by morrow) and "letter" (named by you; it is transcript.jsonl). Click one: the chat changes, the URL says ?chat=<id>, the kanban stays the same, because the board is shared. Each card names the chat it came from.

Press "+ new chat" (or type /chat new) and send "Task: call the pharmacy about the receipts." in it. The card appears on the shared kanban, dashed and tagged with the new chat, and after the first reply the chat gets a name from the title role (model · morrow). /chat rename <title> names it yourself.
Click the chat tag on a card (e.g. "invoices" on task-9): that chat opens and scrolls to the message the card came from. /why task-9 cites chats/c-invoices.jsonl and its line.

Open {url}/?chat=c-invoices in a second tab: each tab stays in its own chat, and a card added in one appears on the board in both. Alt+S focuses the sidebar (arrows, Enter; Escape back). Below 900 px the sidebar is a drawer: the ☰ button in the title bar. "archived: 1" at the bottom shows the archived chat; nothing is ever deleted ({dir}/chats/).
